title: Console Explorer: intermittent metric series pruning in long-running aggregates causes missing panels in incidents
creator: Ravi Patel
description:
Summary: Several customers (notably a Dedicated / Private customer during a high-traffic incident) reported missing time-series in Console Explorer and broken dashboard panels during incident triage. Missing series also caused trace <-> metric correlation links to appear incomplete. This ticket tracks the root cause investigation, immediate mitigation, and the follow-up engineering fixes and observability improvements.

Root cause hypothesis: TTL-based pruning/compaction logic in the metric aggregator incorrectly computed retention for high-cardinality tag sets when compaction ran against long-running aggregate windows. In Private/Dedicated deployments the nightly compaction job combines shards differently, and a race with the series tombstone marker caused series to be marked for early deletion. When series were pruned, Explorer queries returned empty series or partial shards which the Console UI treated as a panel error. Tracing service continued to ingest spans but the metric series IDs (used to correlate traces) were reclaimed, breaking trace links.

Impact observed: Missing panels and gaps on key SLO dashboards during incidents, delayed incident response for customers, and at least two customer escalations in the last 72 hours. Reproduced on a staging Private deployment with synthetic high-cardinality load.

Investigation notes and artifacts: See links below (Confluence incident notes, repro script, dashboards). Key logs show compactor job logging: "compact: evicting series id=%d reason=ttl_pruned" shortly after a shard rollover. Heap/GC metrics on the compactor host indicate periodic CPU spikes aligning with compaction windows.

Decision and plan: 1) Deploy a hotfix that changes compactor to use conservative retention logic (defer tombstone reclamation by 24h) and disables an aggressive shard collapse optimization in Private/Dedicated runs. 2) Add a short-term Console-side guard: if an Explorer query returns an unexpectedly empty series set for high-cardinality metrics, surface a fallback to fetch raw series from the primary ingest nodes. 3) Long-term: rewrite compactor retention checks to be idempotent and add stronger unit/e2e tests and an isolation test harness.

Postmortem follow-ups: Expand alerting for sudden series-count drops, add a canary job to validate compactor behavior after deploys, and update runbooks for incidents that include a checklist for checking compactor and shard-alignment.
steps_to_reproduce: Provision a Private deployment with default compaction enabled and add a synthetic workload that emits 200k distinct series over 6 hours (tags include user.device_id and request_id).
Trigger manual compaction/shard rollover via the admin API at t+6h.
Query Console Explorer for the high-cardinality metric with a 1h window centered on the compaction time and observe missing/empty series set.
Cross-check compactor logs on the host that ran compaction and confirm 'ttl_pruned' entries immediately before missing panels appear.
mitigation_actions: Rolled out hotfix to staging (metric-aggregator PR #5210) that defers tombstone reclamation by 24h and disables aggressive shard-collapsing on Private/Dedicated nodes.
Added temporary Console fallback that fetches raw series from ingest nodes when Explorer returns < 5 series for an otherwise expected set.
Opened alert: OBS_SERIES_DROP with 10m burn-in to notify on >40% series-count reduction for a metric in a 15m window.
